key_insight: TDFold reframes 3D protein structure prediction as a 2D image‑like diffusion task using geometric templates, enabling accurate reconstruction of protein folds from single sequences with markedly improved speed and efficiency.
problem_solved: Reduces reliance on expensive multiple-sequence alignments and heavy 3D optimization by enabling accurate, fast structure prediction directly from single amino‑acid sequences.
method: Encode 3D geometry as 2D image‑like geometric templates (e.g., distance/angle maps) suitable for diffusion modeling.
Apply a 2D diffusion/denoising network over these templates to iteratively refine geometric priors toward a consistent protein fold.
Decode refined 2D templates back into 3D coordinates with an efficient inference pipeline, trading costly 3D operations for lightweight 2D processing.
impact: Makes high-quality protein structure prediction more accessible and scalable for tasks with limited homologous data, accelerating protein design and downstream ML workflows that need rapid, low-cost structural priors.
